attacks.claim: Any SES error, including throttling, records every recipient in the batch as a permanent failure. Those recipients are excluded from the rest of the issue and shown to publishers as 'Not delivered'. There is no retry or backoff. With 48 workers against a 300 msg/s limit, throttling is likely, so real subscribers would be permanently dropped.
attacks.evidence: "if err != nil { for _, r := range batch.Recipients { failures.Record(...) } ... continue }" and "those recipients are excluded from the issue's remaining sends"

attacks.claim: The QA results (0 failures, 11 min) were produced with SES throttling simulated off. Staging used 4 workers, while prod uses 48 workers at about 25 msg/s each, roughly 1200 msg/s of demand against a 300 msg/s limit. Production behavior under throttling is unproven. The QA run also took 11 min against a goal of under 3 min.
attacks.evidence: "QA ran with SES throttling simulated off via the sandbox mock"; "SEND_WORKERS=48"; "300 messages/second"; "~25 msg/s sustained"

attacks.claim: The launch post tells all publishers that Smart Send is live for every publication today. The rollout plan ramps it 5%, 25%, then 100% over three weeks, gated on metrics, while the prod config already sets the default to on. The public announcement contradicts the gated plan and cannot be retracted.
attacks.evidence: "Smart Send Time is live for every publication today" vs "5% (week 1), 25% (week 2), 100% (week 3)" and "SMART_SEND_DEFAULT=on"

attacks.claim: The 'up to 5× faster' claim is unsupported. Staging shows 11 min against a 14 min baseline, about 1.3x, and there is no prod measurement.
attacks.evidence: "every Inkwell issue reaches inboxes up to 5× faster" vs "Pass, 0 failures, 11 min"

attacks.claim: Smart Send holds issues for up to 18 hours by default. 40% of publications are news outlets with time-sensitive content, and no per-issue urgency override is described. The default harms the core use case, and the top request (time-zone scheduling) has already shipped.
attacks.evidence: "Issues are held for at most 18 hours. Enabled by default for all publications" and "4,480 of them (40%) are news or local-news outlets"

attacks.claim: The error path skips Ack after already recording failures, so a redelivered batch is both marked failed and retried. The per-entry loop indexes batch.Recipients[i] with no length check against the result count, so a mismatch would panic or misattribute failures.
attacks.evidence: "continue" with no q.Ack on the error path; "batch.Recipients[i].SubscriberID" with no length check

attacks.claim: The batch-failure metric and 'Not delivered' volume are dashboard-only. The pager covers only queue lag and complaint rate, so a throttling-driven delivery loss would not page anyone. There is no alert on the Smart Send hold backlog either.
attacks.evidence: "On-call pager: queue lag > 10 min, complaint rate > 0.1%"; send.batch_failed listed only under Dashboards

attacks.claim: There is no client-side rate limiter or per-publication quota. One large issue, or a burst across 11,240 publications, can saturate the shared 300 msg/s and 25M/day SES limits and starve other publishers. Smart Send hour-aligned delivery also concentrates load into peak hours.
attacks.evidence: "SES production account limits (us-east-1): 300 messages/second, 25M/day" with no limiter in the loop or config

attacks.claim: The pipeline deploys to 100% of sends with no canary. Smart Send rollback releases all held issues at once, creating a burst into the SES limits, and under the current error handling a burst that triggers throttling would permanently fail recipients.
attacks.evidence: "deploy Monday 09:00 UTC to 100% of sends"; "held issues are released immediately"

attacks.claim: Smart Send builds a per-subscriber behavioral profile from 90 days of opens, on by default. No subscriber notice, retention limit or opt-out for readers is described.
attacks.evidence: "predicts each subscriber's most likely open hour from their last 90 days of opens"

attacks.claim: Default-on behavioral profiling has no documented lawful basis or legal review (GDPR/ePrivacy-style), and delaying election or weather alerts raises public-interest concerns. Neither is assessed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no legal or consent assessment; "Enabled by default for all publications"

attacks.claim: The 71% accuracy figure has no baseline, such as a fixed hour, so it does not show the feature adds value. The 'control' in the ramp gate is undefined.
Sending depends on a single provider (SES) in a single region. The only fallback is the idle Sidekiq sender, which presumably also depends on SES, and its 14-day window is short.
attacks.evidence: "SES_REGION=us-east-1"; "keep the Sidekiq sender deployed but idle for 14 days"

attacks.claim: There is no SES spend estimate or retry budget, though the planned retry fix would increase send volume.
